title: How IB Moderation Affects IA Marks
summary: IB moderation can raise, lower, or preserve IA marks. Learn how sampling, adjustments, weighting, and grade boundaries affect your final IB grade.
body_markdown:
A student opens their results and notices something unsettling: the internal assessment mark does not seem to match the one discussed at school. The first thought is often personal. *Was my work marked down? Was there a mistake?*


The direct answer is that **IB moderation can raise, lower, or leave IA marks unchanged** . Teachers mark internal assessments first. The IB then reviews a sample of work from the school to determine whether the teacher applied the assessment criteria at the expected standard. If the sample indicates that marking was too generous or too severe, an adjustment may be applied to the relevant marks from that school.


That does not necessarily mean an examiner individually remarked every student's IA. Moderation is primarily a quality-control process designed to make internally awarded marks comparable across schools.


### IB moderation at a glance


The process can be reduced to five ideas:


- Your teacher marks your IA using the subject criteria.
- The school submits marks and a selected sample of student work.
- IB examiners review that sample against the same criteria.
- The school's IA marks may be raised, lowered, or left unchanged.
- The moderated IA result is weighted alongside the externally assessed components when the subject grade is calculated.


The distinction between a **raw IA mark** , a **moderated mark** , a **weighted contribution** , and a **final IB grade** matters. They are connected, but they are not interchangeable.


A student asks a calculator for a grade while it produces an enormous flowchart


### A student tries to follow the mark


Imagine Maya, a hypothetical Diploma Programme student receiving results in July 2026. Her teacher had awarded her IA 18 marks out of a possible 24. Maya expects that number to appear unchanged in the final calculation.


But 18 is the teacher-awarded mark, not a guarantee of the final moderated mark. Her work may or may not have been included in the sample sent to the IB. Even if it was not sampled, an adjustment established through the sample can affect her mark.


The important unit of analysis is therefore not always one isolated student. Moderation examines the standard of marking represented by the school's sample.


This is easier to understand when the process is separated into stages.


Stage What happens


Teacher assessment The teacher marks each IA using the published criteria.


Sampling Work representing the school's range of marks is submitted for review.


Examiner review An IB examiner assesses the sample against the required standard.


Moderation The school's marks may be adjusted when the sample shows a marking difference.


Weighting The moderated IA mark is converted into its weighted contribution to the subject total.


Grade award The combined subject result is compared with the applicable grade boundaries.


The IB's official[assessment guide for teachers and coordinators](https://ibo.org/contentassets/4d92e48d38a4415a87e11555e143a39f/assessment-guide-for-teachers-and-coordinators-en.pdf) explains that a school's marks may be lowered, raised, or remain the same after moderation.


### Why an IA mark can move


Moderation is not intended to punish a school or reward another one. Its purpose is comparability.


Suppose one teacher interprets a criterion generously while another interprets it strictly. Without moderation, two pieces of work at the same standard might receive different marks simply because they were produced in different classrooms. The moderation process attempts to correct that inconsistency.


A simple adjustment might appear to move marks in a broadly consistent direction. In practice, however, moderation can account for differences across the mark range. If marking is accurate near the middle but generous at the top, the treatment does not have to resemble a single identical subtraction from every mark.


There are also limits at the top and bottom of a component's available mark range. A moderated result cannot exceed the component maximum or fall below its minimum.


For Maya, the lesson is subtle. A changed mark does not by itself prove that her teacher was careless, that the examiner disliked her topic, or that her individual IA was singled out. It indicates that the finalized mark reflects the IB's standardized assessment process rather than the teacher's judgment alone.


### Sampled work and unsampled work


One common misunderstanding is that only sampled students are affected by IB moderation. That is not generally how the process works.


The sample is evidence used to evaluate the school's marking standard for the component. Once the IB establishes an appropriate adjustment, it can be applied beyond the sampled scripts. This is why a student whose work was not selected may still receive a moderated result.


If the initial sample does not provide enough evidence for a fair decision, the IB may request additional work. The aim is to establish a defensible adjustment, not to infer an entire school's marking pattern from inadequate evidence.


Students normally cannot control whether their work is sampled. What they can control is the quality and clarity of the submitted work. Revision should therefore focus on meeting each criterion explicitly rather than trying to predict the mechanics of sampling. RevisionDojo's Coursework Library and Tutors can help students understand what criterion-based academic work looks like, while grading tools can highlight weaknesses before school submission. Teacher feedback and the rules governing permitted assistance must always remain the final guide.


### Moderated marks are not IB grades


Maya's next mistake is to treat every lost IA mark as a lost subject grade. The mathematics is rarely that direct.


An IA usually contributes only part of the subject result. Its moderated mark is scaled according to the component weighting, then combined with the weighted results from the other assessed components. In general terms:

If moderation changed the mark from 18 to 17, the contribution would become approximately 14.17. The effect on the combined subject total would therefore be about 0.83 percentage points, not an automatic one-grade fall.


Actual component weights and maximum marks depend on the subject, level, and applicable assessment specification. Students should use the correct guide for their examination session rather than treating this example as a universal formula.


### Where IB grade boundaries enter the story


After the moderated and externally assessed components have been weighted and combined, the resulting total is interpreted using the applicable **IB grade boundaries** . These thresholds convert the final subject total into one of the seven IB grades.


This means the practical effect of an IA adjustment depends partly on where the combined result sits relative to a boundary. A small decrease may change nothing if the total remains securely within the same grade band. The same decrease could matter considerably if the total was close to the next threshold. An upward adjustment can work in the opposite direction.


Grade boundaries are not something students should assume will remain identical across subjects or examination sessions. Comparing a May result with an old November boundary, or one subject with another, can create false certainty.


For Maya, the sensible question is no longer, *Did my IA lose one mark?* It is, *How did the moderated and weighted contribution affect my total under the correct boundaries?*


Use RevisionDojo's Grade boundaries tool for **exact conversions** for the relevant subject and session. That is more reliable than attempting to reconstruct a final grade from a remembered classroom mark.


### What students and parents should do


Before results, the best protection is disciplined preparation. Students can use RevisionDojo's Study Notes and Flashcards to secure subject knowledge, the Questionbank and Predicted Papers to practise assessment decisions, and Mock Exams to identify weak areas under timed conditions. AI Chat can help unpack confusing concepts, while grading tools can provide structured feedback during revision.


For the IA itself, keep the focus narrower:


- Work from the current subject guide and criteria.
- Make evidence for each criterion easy to identify.
- Follow school deadlines and academic integrity requirements.
- Keep drafts and teacher feedback organized.
- Do not assume that a teacher-awarded mark is the finalized IB mark.


After results, avoid reverse-engineering the outcome from incomplete numbers. Ask the school or DP coordinator what component information is available and what formal review options may apply. Schools manage communication with the IB, including any permitted results enquiries. A student or parent should not assume that a review will necessarily increase a mark, because outcomes can depend on the relevant procedure and evidence.


### The mark is a process, not a verdict


By the end of Maya's calculation, the changed number feels less mysterious. It is still consequential, but it is no longer arbitrary. Her teacher assessed the work, a sample tested the school's standard, moderation established comparability, component weighting determined the IA's contribution, and grade boundaries converted the combined total into a subject grade.


That chain is exactly why one classroom mark cannot tell the whole story.

When results arrive, use the Grade boundaries tool for exact conversions rather than guessing what a moderated IA mark means for the final grade.
